summary.headline: Broad risk-off session (SPY -1.52%, QQQ -2.04%) the morning after the Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% with a rare 3-dissent hawkish split, plus a dense earnings/macro cluster: QCOM missed on EPS with margin pressure and a cut Apple-revenue outlook (-4.40% into an additional after-hours slide to $143.77); LRCX and GD both beat and raised guidance (LRCX Q4 beat, FY guide well above Street; GD record $136.5B backlog, +32% YoY) but fell anyway (-6.49% and -2.96%) as the broader AI-infrastructure complex was hit by 'monstrous, motivated, margined' selling (AMD -5.58%, MRVL -6.29%, CRDO -7.61%, NXPI -6.86%) -- notably, the standing hyperscaler-capex watch actually resolved favorably overnight (MSFT beat with steady capex guidance, META raised FY guidance), meaning today's chip-complex selloff is a positioning/deleveraging move, not a capex-guidance-driven repricing. Bitcoin-miner/AI-datacenter names got hit hardest on capex-financing-appetite concerns unrelated to Bitcoin's price (HUT -12.80%, MARA -11.63%). CAT -6.97% on no identified catalyst (earnings not until 8/4) -- flagged as an unexplained silent decliner. CWAN roster-integrity flag: unresolved for a 31st day; the 'fixed in this run's commit' claim has now failed 3 runs straight -- flagging as a pipeline bug this time instead of re-asserting the same fix worked.

flags.headline: QCOM misses EPS, cuts Apple revenue outlook, announces defensive price hikes -- escalated from yesterday's pre-earnings AMBER
flags.detail: Qualcomm reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $9.9B (in line, high end of guide) but non-GAAP EPS of $2.21 missed the $2.23 consensus. Shares closed the regular session down 4.40-4.49%, then slid an additional ~7.65% after hours to $143.77 on investor concern over near-term margin pressure. The report confirmed a sharp drop in the Apple-related QCT revenue outlook and continued Chinese handset-market softness; CEO Cristiano Amon announced across-the-board chip price increases effective September 1 as a margin defense. Automotive was a bright spot (record $1.6B revenue, +61% YoY) but did not offset the core-chip concerns.
flags.thesis_link: Directly matches two listed QCOM key_risks simultaneously: 'Chinese customer weakness drove QCT revenue down... if recovery is slower than management's timeline, revenue growth could remain subdued' and 'Apple modem internalization -- if Apple successfully develops in-house baseband modems, Qualcomm could lose its largest QCT customer.' This is a real earnings-driven confirmation of both risks, not sector sympathy.

flags.headline: HUT -12.80%, sharply escalated from persisting AMBER on AI-datacenter capex/financing concerns, not Bitcoin price
flags.detail: Hut 8 fell 12.80% ($88.17 vs $101.11) in the broader Bitcoin-miner-to-AI-datacenter group selloff. Per CNBC, the driver is 'concern around capex requirements and whether companies across the miner-to-AI group may need to raise incremental capital at higher costs to fund their development pipelines,' with investors questioning whether 'credit appetite for these projects is approaching its limits' -- not a Bitcoin-price move. Riot, CleanSpark, Core Scientific and Cipher Mining all fell in sympathy the same session.
flags.thesis_link: Directly matches HUT's own listed key_risk: '$3.25B in secured debt for data center construction creates leverage risk if projects face delays, cost overruns, or if AI infrastructure demand moderates from current elevated expectations.' Today's move is that risk being actively repriced by the market, not a rumor.

flags.detail: Marathon (MARA) fell 11.63% ($10.07 vs $11.395) in the same miner-to-AI-datacenter selloff described under HUT -- market questioning capex funding and credit appetite for the sector's AI pivot, not a Bitcoin-price-specific move.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA's listed key_risk: 'AI infrastructure pivot competes against hyperscalers... with dramatically greater scale, capital, and customer relationships' -- today's selloff is the market pricing exactly that competitive/funding disadvantage.

flags.headline: LRCX -6.49% despite a Q4 beat and a guide well above Street -- good report, bad tape
flags.detail: Lam Research beat Q4 FY2026 estimates (adj. EPS $1.82 vs $1.68 est; revenue $6.72B vs $6.67B est; 51.7% gross margin) and guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $7.70-8.50B and EPS to $2.00-2.30, both well above the ~$7.09B / $1.83 Street consensus. Despite that, shares fell 6.49% in the broader AI-infrastructure-equipment selloff. This is important nuance: LRCX's fundamentals and forward guidance actually strengthened the thesis today -- the decline is macro/sector positioning, not a company-specific miss.
flags.thesis_link: Does NOT match a materializing key_risk -- if anything this print argues against the 'AI infrastructure spending deceleration' key_risk in the near term. Kept RED on price-action magnitude for desk visibility, but flagged explicitly as a fundamentals-improving, price-declining divergence.
